newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Attorney General to sue tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Attorney General to sue tobacco companies.

text.p: Illinois Attorney General Jim Ryan said on Tuesday he had decided to sue tobacco companies to recover state taxpayers' portion of the billions of dollars the state has paid in smoking-related health care costs.
Fifteen states have already filed suit against the tobacco industry to recover Medeicaid costs.

"I believe the state can prove in court that the tobacco companies engaged in misrepresentation, omission of material fact, deception and conspiracy that ultimately shortened lives and shortchanged taxpayers," Ryan said in a statement.
From 1980 to 1993, the state of Illinois incurred $2.75 billion in health care costs for services provided to Medicaid recipients attributable to smoking, he said.
"I have determined that the state has solid legal grounds to file this lawsuit," he said. "We will pursue it with all our vigor."
The decision to sue followed a review initiated in March by the attorney general's office of documents and legal research and included meetings with other attorneys general.
Illinois will be the sixteenth state to sue tobacco firms.
In coming weeks, Ryan said he will announce a team of local and national law firms to assist in the case. The firms will be required to bear most of the costs of the litigation, he said.
Alternative sources of funding also are being explored to limit the expenditure of tax dollars, he added.
Ryan said the suit would seek to recover some or all of the health care costs.
The suit is expected to be filed by the end of the year, according to a spokesman for the attorney general's office.

No specific names were disclosed but defendants named in suits by other states include: Philip Morris Cos Inc ; RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co; Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp and its parent, B A T Industries Plc ; Loews Corp's Lorillard Tobacco Co; the Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group Inc; UST Inc's United States Tobacco Co; the Council of Tobacco Research U.S.A. Inc and the Tobacco Institute Inc, among others.
